worked_solution:
A numerical method has order $p$ if $p$ is the largest positive integer such that the local truncation error (LTE) satisfies

$$
τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{p+1})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

The order describes how fast errors shrink as $Δx$ decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order $p$ if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of $k$ reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately ${k}^{p+1}.$

First, we compute the LTE for the given step sizes:

- With step size $Δx=0.5,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.5) & =8(0.5)^{5}+2(0.5)^{6} \\  & =8\cdot 0.031\,25+2\cdot 0.015\,625 \\  & =0.281\,25 \\  & ≈0.281.\end{aligned}
$$

- With step size $Δx=0.2,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.2) & =8(0.2)^{5}+2(0.2)^{6} \\  & =8\cdot 0.000\,32+2\cdot 0.000\,064 \\  & =0.002\,688 \\  & ≈0.003.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from $0.5$ to $0.2.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
k=\frac{0.5}{0.2}=2.5.
$$

As a result, for a numerical method of order $p,$ the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately

$$
{k}^{p+1}={2.5}^{p+1}.
$$

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from $0.281\,25$ to $0.002\,688.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
\frac{0.281\,25}{0.002\,688}=104.631\,69…≈104.632.
$$

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{2.5}^{p+1} & ≈104.631\,69… \\ p+1 & ≈{log}_{2.5}⁡(104.631\,69…) \\ p+1 & ≈5.075… \\ p & ≈4.075….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is
$4.$

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the LTE:

$$
τ(Δx)=8(Δx)^{5}+2(Δx)^{6}\,⇒\,τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{5})=O\,((Δx)^{4+1}),\,Δx\to 0.
$$

Hence, the order of the method is $4.$

In other words, a numerical method has order p if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of k reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately kp+1.

First, we compute the LTE for the given step sizes:

  • With step size Δx=0.5, the LTE is τ(0.5)=8(0.5)5+2(0.5)6=8⋅0.03125+2⋅0.015625=0.28125≈0.281.

  • With step size Δx=0.2, the LTE is τ(0.2)=8(0.2)5+2(0.2)6=8⋅0.00032+2⋅0.000064=0.002688≈0.003.

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from 0.5 to 0.2. So, it reduces by a factor of k=0.50.2=2.5.

As a result, for a numerical method of order p, the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately kp+1=2.5p+1.

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from 0.28125 to 0.002688. So, it reduces by a factor of 0.281250.002688=104.63169…≈104.632.

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get 2.5p+1≈104.63169…p+1≈log2.5⁡(104.63169…)p+1≈5.075…p≈4.075….

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is 4.

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the LTE: τ(Δx)=8(Δx)5+2(Δx)6⇒τ(Δx)=O((Δx)5)=O((Δx)4+1),Δx→0. Hence, the order of the method is 4.
